links.outcome: Expert-rated safety and hallucination-free rates for retrieval-augmented versus general-purpose LLMs
links.effect: OpenEvidence (medical RAG) had 100% safe and 100% hallucination-free responses; general-purpose safe rates 56.7%-86.7% and hallucination-free rates 36.7%-93.3% (Cochran's Q p<0.01).
links.quote: Across 330 responses (1320 ratings), OpenEvidence achieved 100% safe and 100% hallucination-free responses.

links.outcome: Hallucinations in general-purpose LLM outputs on dental implant complications rated by blinded experts
links.effect: Hallucination-free rates among general-purpose platforms ranged from 36.7% (Claude 4.5 Haiku) to 93.3% (GPT-5.4 Thinking; Qwen 3.5-Plus), a significant difference.
links.quote: Among general-purpose platforms, safe rates ranged from 56.7% (Claude 4.5 Haiku) to 86.7% (Perplexity) and hallucination-free rates from 36.7% (Claude 4.5 Haiku) to 93.3% (GPT-5.4 Thinking; Qwen 3.5-Plus), both significant (Cochran's Q, p < 0.01).

screen.reason: Empirical study comparing expert-rated clinical accuracy, safety, and hallucination rates across general-purpose LLMs and retrieval-augmented platforms (RAG) using clinical vignettes.
